title: Evaluation of X-Ray Imaging Techniques for Enhanced Tissue Diagnostics
summary:
This study investigates new X-ray imaging methods that may allow better detection of pathological changes in human tissue. Conventional X-ray techniques such as radiography, angiography, and CT often cannot visualize soft tissue structures in sufficient detail.
We will therefore test novel approaches, including dark-field and phase-contrast imaging, high-resolution X-ray sources, and spectral methods. These techniques promise sharper, more detailed images while potentially reducing radiation exposure.
Human tissue samples containing both healthy and pathological tissue will be analyzed. The new X-ray images will be compared with standard histological stainings from pathology to assess their diagnostic value. The goal is to significantly improve image quality and open up new possibilities for more precise diagnostics in medicine.
conditions: Healthy and pathologically altered tissue samples will be examined.

interventions.name: Human tissue samples imaged with novel X-ray techniques (dark-field, phase-contrast, monoenergetic imaging, nano-CT, spectral imaging), compared with established clinical imaging modalities.
